source.description:
Layer: boundary
Strategy: DI-injected unit tests (repo convention, mirrors cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts) as primary, plus one recorded-fixture contract test using a real captured OpenRouter response sample. Live tests against the real API are not run in CI (no committed OPENROUTER_API_KEY) — this is the documented live-first fallback.
Covers: xtrm-2azdj.1

What implementation it covers: fetchBenchmarks, readCache/writeCache, refreshBenchmarks orchestration in cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts.

Test file structure: cli/src/tests/model-benchmarks.test.ts, mirroring cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts's pattern (inject cacheFile via mkdtempSync, now via fixed clock, fetchFn as a plain fake function — no HTTP-mocking library).

Assertions required:
- [ ] Cold cache (file absent) → refreshBenchmarks calls the injected fetchFn and writes the cache file with the fetched data + fetchedAt.
- [ ] Fresh cache (within TTL) → does NOT call fetchFn; returns cached data as-is.
- [ ] Expired cache → calls fetchFn again; on success, overwrites the cache entry and timestamp.
- [ ] fetchFn throws/rejects → existing cache file (if any) is left untouched; refreshBenchmarks surfaces a clear typed error, does not write partial/garbage data.
- [ ] Missing OPENROUTER_API_KEY (injected as absent) → clear typed error before any network attempt; fetchFn is never invoked in this path.
- [ ] Cache write failure (e.g. unwritable directory) → does not throw out of refreshBenchmarks (best-effort-swallow semantics matching npm-latest.ts:59-66); caller still receives the freshly fetched data even though persistence failed.
- [ ] Recorded-fixture contract check: a committed fixture file (e.g. cli/src/tests/fixtures/openrouter-benchmarks-sample.json) containing a real captured response shape (obtained manually during xtrm-2azdj.1 implementation with a personal API key, NOT a live call in the test itself) is parsed by the module's type/parsing logic and asserted to produce the expected typed cache entries — this catches drift between the assumed field names (model_permaslug, agentic_index, coding_index, intelligence_index, pricing.prompt, pricing.completion) and the module's actual parsing code, without requiring network access in CI.

Fixture policy:
- [ ] No shared mutable state — each test gets its own mkdtempSync directory.
- [ ] Deterministic `now` injection — no bare Date.now() in the test.

Anti-pattern check:
- [ ] Not over-mocked: fetchFn is a plain injected function per the module's own DI design (matches the repo's existing convention for exactly this kind of external call), not a patch of an internal collaborator.

Critical paths covered:
- Cache-miss vs cache-hit branching — risk: an off-by-one in TTL comparison silently causes either constant unnecessary network calls or permanently stale data.
- API-key-absent short-circuit — risk: an unauthenticated request would either fail with a confusing error deep in the fetch call or, worse, silently succeed against a public/free endpoint with wrong data.
- Recorded-fixture schema check — risk: this epic's rank/compare/recommend field-name assumptions were explicitly flagged as unverified in xtrm-2azdj's CONSTRAINTS; if the real API shape differs, this is the one test that would catch it before it reaches production.

Known deferred paths:
- True live-network contract test (hitting the real OpenRouter endpoint) — deferred because no committed API key exists in this repo. Follow-up: if the team later adds a CI-safe test API key/secret, create a `@live`-tagged test that supersedes the recorded fixture as primary evidence (to be created — no bd issue yet, note this in xtrm-2azdj's epic notes at close).

Debuggability evidence required: refreshBenchmarks failure paths should be catchable with the injected fetchFn's rejection reason surfacing unchanged in the thrown/returned error (test asserts the error message/type, not just "it throws").

Done when: all assertions pass in `npm test --workspace cli`, and the recorded-fixture file is committed alongside the test.
source.title: Test: benchmark cache module — DI unit tests + recorded-fixture contract check
